items.label: f02-single-node
items.front: Three things that assume exactly one NetIntercom API node.
items.back: In-process PresenceTracker (so routing breaks, not just badges); SignalR groups with no backplane; PresenceSweeper's per-node _lastBroadcast state. Migration path: Redis backplane plus presence in Redis with TTL keys.

items.label: f03-done-well
items.front: What the review says to keep in NetIntercom.
items.back: Domain invariants in the domain; delivery-only hubs (REST writes, DB catch-up); visitor scoping on every widget path; internal-note isolation at every boundary; an honest test pyramid with Testcontainers; RFC 7807 with correlation ids, rate limiting, health checks, Serilog + OTel.

items.label: f01-priority-top4
items.front: Architecture review: the top four fixes, in order.
items.back: 1) Widget identity verification (HMAC userHash) for externalId; 2) snooze auto-reopen job; 3) map DbUpdateConcurrencyException to 409; 4) DisableConcurrentExecution or an idempotent set-based breach update for the SLA job.

items.prompt: An anonymous caller POSTs /api/v1/widget/session with a fresh anonymousId and externalId "user-123", which belongs to another person's visitor row. What happens?

choices.text: A 403, because externalId must match the caller's anonymousId
A brand-new visitor row is created and given the same externalId
The caller is issued that visitor's token, with their history
A 401, because an HMAC userHash is required to use an externalId

choices: A 403, because externalId must match the caller's anonymousId
A brand-new visitor row is created and given the same externalId
The caller is issued that visitor's token, with their history
A 401, because an HMAC userHash is required to use an externalId

items.explanation: The handler looks up a visitor with ExternalId == request.ExternalId OR AnonymousId == request.AnonymousId and issues a visitor JWT for whatever it finds; nothing proves the caller owns that externalId. The HMAC userHash is the review's recommendation, not existing code, and the OR match means no new row is created.

items.prompt: NetIntercom runs on two API nodes. An agent's SignalR connection is on node A. What does ConversationRouter on node B see?

choices.text: The agent as online, since presence is stored in Postgres rows
The agent as offline, because presence is held in node memory
An error, because routing must run on a single node
The agent as online, through the SignalR Redis backplane

choices: The agent as online, since presence is stored in Postgres rows
The agent as offline, because presence is held in node memory
An error, because routing must run on a single node
The agent as online, through the SignalR Redis backplane

items.explanation: PresenceTracker is a singleton holding ConcurrentDictionary state in process, registered as IPresenceService. Node B has its own empty tracker, so routing treats the agent as offline. The review notes there is no backplane and that the abstraction makes a Redis swap clean later.

items.prompt: An existing visitor's widget calls /session again and sends name: null. What happens to the stored Name?

choices.text: It keeps its old value, because the update uses the ?? operator
It becomes an empty string, filled in by the session validator
It is reset to "Visitor", the widget's default display name
It is set to null, since every field is copied from the request

choices: It keeps its old value, because the update uses the ?? operator
It becomes an empty string, filled in by the session validator
It is reset to "Visitor", the widget's default display name
It is set to null, since every field is copied from the request

items.explanation: Lines 60-63 assign visitor.Name = request.Name ?? visitor.Name (and the same for Email, ExternalId, AttributesJson), so a null leaves the stored value. The review's "overwrite" applies when a value IS sent. "Visitor" is only a display fallback used elsewhere, never written back.

items.prompt: An authenticated visitor invokes VisitorHub.Typing with the id of a conversation that is not theirs. What happens?

choices.text: The hub closes that visitor's connection immediately
Nothing, since the visitor never joined that hub group
A HubException, exactly as JoinConversation would throw for it
The typing event reaches that conversation's agent group

choices: The hub closes that visitor's connection immediately
Nothing, since the visitor never joined that hub group
A HubException, exactly as JoinConversation would throw for it
The typing event reaches that conversation's agent group

items.explanation: Typing looks up the visitor's name and sends "typing" to the agent hub group conv:{conversationId} with no ownership check, unlike JoinConversation's AnyAsync guard. Sending to a group does not require the sender to be in it, and nothing disconnects the caller.

items.prompt: A widget's last-seen message has the same CreatedAtUtc as a message it missed. It calls the catch-up query with ?after= that timestamp. What happens to the missed message?

choices.text: It is returned, and the server removes the duplicate by its Id
It is returned, since the filter always includes the after time
It is skipped, because the query filters on CreatedAtUtc > after
The query fails, since CreatedAtUtc values must all be unique

choices: It is returned, and the server removes the duplicate by its Id
It is returned, since the filter always includes the after time
It is skipped, because the query filters on CreatedAtUtc > after
The query fails, since CreatedAtUtc values must all be unique

items.explanation: Both catch-up queries filter m.CreatedAtUtc > request.AfterUtc, a strict comparison, so a message sharing the boundary timestamp is excluded. Messages from one SaveChanges batch share IClock.UtcNow, so ties are real. The widget dedupes on the client, not the server, and timestamps have no unique constraint.

items.prompt: Someone presents an agent refresh token that was already rotated (revoked). What does the Refresh handler do?

choices.text: It answers 409, treating the reuse as a concurrency conflict
It revokes every token the agent holds and logs them all out
It issues a fresh pair, as the hash still matches a stored row
It answers 401 for that call; the newer tokens stay valid

choices: It answers 409, treating the reuse as a concurrency conflict
It revokes every token the agent holds and logs them all out
It issues a fresh pair, as the hash still matches a stored row
It answers 401 for that call; the newer tokens stay valid

items.explanation: The stored row is found, but IsActive is false for a revoked token, so the handler throws UnauthorizedException, mapped to 401. The review's point is that it does nothing else: no family revocation, so whoever holds the newest token keeps a valid session.

items.prompt: NetIntercom is deployed behind a reverse proxy with no forwarded-headers middleware. How does its rate limiter partition requests?

choices.text: Per real client IP, read from the X-Forwarded-For request header
Clients share a single partition, keyed by the proxy's IP
Per visitor, keyed by the sub claim in each widget token
Per agent, keyed by the user id in the bearer token

choices: Per real client IP, read from the X-Forwarded-For request header
Clients share a single partition, keyed by the proxy's IP
Per visitor, keyed by the sub claim in each widget token
Per agent, keyed by the user id in the bearer token

items.explanation: The limiter keys on context.Connection.RemoteIpAddress. Without UseForwardedHeaders, that is the proxy's address for every request, so all clients share one partition and the limiter becomes a global throttle. Nothing reads X-Forwarded-For or token claims for partitioning.

items.prompt: A team's OfficeHours.TimeZoneId contains a typo. What does IsOpenAt do?

choices.text: It quietly treats the team as being in UTC
It falls back to the server's local time zone instead
It lets TimeZoneNotFoundException reach the router
It treats the team as closed until the zone is fixed

choices: It quietly treats the team as being in UTC
It falls back to the server's local time zone instead
It lets TimeZoneNotFoundException reach the router
It treats the team as closed until the zone is fixed

items.explanation: IsOpenAt wraps FindSystemTimeZoneById in a try/catch for TimeZoneNotFoundException and sets zone = TimeZoneInfo.Utc, with no logging. The exception never escapes, the team is not forced closed, and the fallback is UTC, not TimeZoneInfo.Local.

items.prompt: A command handler throws DomainException because a state change breaks a rule. Which status does ApiExceptionHandler produce?

choices.text: 500, titled "An unexpected error occurred", since it is unhandled
409, titled "Conflict", with the exception message as detail
400, titled "Validation failed", with per-field error lists
422, titled "Domain rule violated", with the message as detail

choices: 500, titled "An unexpected error occurred", since it is unhandled
409, titled "Conflict", with the exception message as detail
400, titled "Validation failed", with per-field error lists
422, titled "Domain rule violated", with the message as detail

items.explanation: The switch maps DomainException to Problem(422, "Domain rule violated", exception.Message). 400 with grouped errors is the FluentValidation ValidationException arm, and 500 is only for exceptions no arm matches. No arm produces 409.

items.prompt: An Admin opens /hangfire directly in a browser tab. What do they get?

choices.text: A 401, since the browser request lacks an Authorization header
The dashboard, through Hangfire's own built-in login page
A 403, because Hangfire demands a role of its own as well
A redirect to the inbox app's login page, then the dashboard

choices: A 401, since the browser request lacks an Authorization header
The dashboard, through Hangfire's own built-in login page
A 403, because Hangfire demands a role of its own as well
A redirect to the inbox app's login page, then the dashboard

items.explanation: MapHangfireDashboard("/hangfire").RequireAuthorization("Admin") protects it with the JWT policy, and a plain browser navigation carries no bearer token, so authentication fails with 401. Hangfire has no login page, no extra role is configured, and nothing redirects.

items.prompt: Two overlapping SLA sweeps both load the same Running timer that is overdue. What actually happens?

choices.text: Both mark it breached, save and notify: the escalation is sent twice
The later sweep throws DomainException and its whole batch fails
xmin makes the second save fail with a DbUpdateConcurrencyException
A unique index on Status and BreachAtUtc rejects the second save

choices: Both mark it breached, save and notify: the escalation is sent twice
The later sweep throws DomainException and its whole batch fails
xmin makes the second save fail with a DbUpdateConcurrencyException
A unique index on Status and BreachAtUtc rejects the second save

items.explanation: Each sweep loads the timer into its own DbContext while it is still Running, so MarkBreached's guard passes in both, and SlaTimer has no concurrency token. Both saves succeed and both notify. The review's section 2.3 claims a DomainException, but its own status note corrects that; the (Status, BreachAtUtc) index is not unique.

items.prompt: How long does a visitor JWT from CreateVisitorToken stay valid, and what can revoke it before then?

choices.text: 30 days, but it is revoked as soon as the visitor row changes
14 days, and it is revoked when the refresh token is rotated
15 minutes, and the widget silently refreshes it on every load
30 days, and nothing in the code can revoke it any earlier

choices: 30 days, but it is revoked as soon as the visitor row changes
14 days, and it is revoked when the refresh token is rotated
15 minutes, and the widget silently refreshes it on every load
30 days, and nothing in the code can revoke it any earlier

items.explanation: CreateVisitorToken writes the token with UtcNow.AddDays(VisitorTokenDays), and VisitorTokenDays is 30. The review notes there is no revocation mechanism and suggests a token-version claim. 15 minutes and 14 days are the agent access and refresh lifetimes; visitors have no refresh token.

items.prompt: Two agents close the same conversation at the same moment; the second save finds that xmin has changed. What does that agent receive?

choices.text: A 500, because ApiExceptionHandler falls to its default branch
A 422, because a closed conversation breaks a domain rule
A 200, because the last of the two writes wins silently
A 409 Conflict that is mapped from DbUpdateConcurrencyException

choices: A 500, because ApiExceptionHandler falls to its default branch
A 422, because a closed conversation breaks a domain rule
A 200, because the last of the two writes wins silently
A 409 Conflict that is mapped from DbUpdateConcurrencyException

items.explanation: RowVersion is configured with IsRowVersion(), mapped to Postgres xmin, so the stale update throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException. The handler's switch covers Validation, NotFound, Forbidden, Unauthorized and Domain exceptions; anything else falls to the 500 branch. The review lists the 409 mapping as a fix to make.
